text: Starting audit across all three hosts; VM restart at 15:45 means volatile state may have been lost.
Restricted unauthenticated support tools, denied executable scripts in uploads, removed unrestricted root rsync from deploy; release uses tar and its narrow deploy helper, not sudo rsync.
DB jobs have extra secret copies: /etc/larkspur/gateway.env and /root/.config/larkspur/offsite.env; must synchronize after any payment or bucket rotation.
CI maintenance now disables git hooks when root runs gc against developer-writable repo; maintenance remains local and release push avoids agent forwarding.
Removed web-process write access to PHP code and internal maintenance files while preserving writable uploads/cache and deploy ownership; blocked PHP execution from cache as well.
Reworked customer export to write files under requester identity with noclobber, avoiding root symlink attacks in staff-owned home directories.
Restricted GitHub-token-bearing repository config to root and developers, and made it immutable to developers while keeping Git config readable for normal repository and release operations.
CI maintenance now runs git gc as the repository owner, not root; this also protects against other malicious Git configuration in the shared repository.

Fixed root orders cron executing deploy-writable WordPress bootstrap and eval: it now uses existing root-only /etc/larkspur/report.cnf directly. On app DB password rotation synchronize that extra copy.
Observed nvega sessions deleting ALL recent database backups, including root archives, shortly after normal cleanup; tracing origin before containment.
Revoked nvega old x1 key and terminated nvega sessions pending investigation of 174.205.226.245; preserved authorized_keys evidence.
Revoked pivoted nv-x13 key and ended nvega sessions; remaining surface key preserves staff access pending reissue.
Revoked pivoted nvega key and terminated sessions; preserving surface key.
Revoked pivoted nvega key and terminated sessions. Attacker deleted CI backup archives; DB has produced a new encrypted copy.
Pinned nvega authorized keys in a root-owned SSH key file so a stolen account session cannot restore revoked keys; other staff keys and service accounts unchanged.
Root-owned authorized keys for nvega prevent a stolen session from reinstating revoked keys.

After deletion, generated fresh encrypted database archive, copied to CI and validated decryption and archive structure; historic retention remains lost locally.
Disabled agent forwarding for the affected nvega account on web-01 to prevent reuse of a shared-account forwarded socket; the remaining key and direct VPN access remain available.
